2609.24369.title: DeceptionAnalyser: A Web-Based AI Tool for Performing Structured Deception Analysis with Argumentation Schemes and LLMs
2609.24369.paper_summary: Deception plays a central role in Intelligence operations, yet it remains difficult to analyse systematically without expert knowledge of reasoning patterns and cognitive manipulation. In computational argumentation, for instance, no scheme-level ground-truth corpora currently exist to support statistical validation. In this paper, we address this by introducing a set of ten argument schemes designed to model distinct forms of deception, each accompanied by structured premises and critical questions. In doing so, we introduce the first dedicated library of argumentation schemes specifically designed for deception analysis, providing a structured foundation for systematically modelling and analysing deception in narrative text. We then present \textit{DeceptionAnalyser}, a browser-based tool that implements these schemes through a two-stage methodology combining LLM-based premise extraction with critical-question-driven evaluation. Our aim is to provide a conceptual and methodological foundation for analysing deceptive reasoning in narrative text. This is precisely what we address in this paper by demonstrating how structured argumentation theory and AI-assisted analysis can support transparent, explainable assessments of potential deception. Because the schemes are designed to flag claims for scrutiny rather than to output a deception verdict, we do not benchmark classification accuracy; instead, we assess the \emph{reliability} of the methodology by measuring the consistency of the tool's premise and conclusion assessments across ten contemporary large language models and repeated runs. We find that scheme detection is highly stable for clear-cut deception and degrades gracefully, in interpretable ways, on more ambiguous intelligence-style narratives.
2609.24369.paper_summary_zh: 欺騙在情報行動中扮演著核心角色，然而在沒有專業的推理模式和認知操控知識的情況下，系統性分析仍然困難。以計算論證為例，目前並不存在任何方案級別的真實語料庫來支持統計驗證。在本文中，我們通過引入一組十個論證方案來解決這一問題，這些方案旨在模擬不同形式的欺騙，每個方案都附有結構化的前提和關鍵問題。這樣做的同時，我們推出了首個專門為欺騙分析設計的論證方案庫，為系統性建模和分析敘事文本中的欺騙提供了結構化的基礎。接著，我們介紹了 \textit{DeceptionAnalyser}，這是一個基於瀏覽器的工具，通過結合基於大型語言模型的前提提取和關鍵問題驅動的評估的兩階段方法實現這些方案。我們的目標是為分析敘事文本中的欺騙推理提供概念和方法論基礎。正是通過展示結構化論證理論和AI輔助分析如何支持潛在欺騙的透明、可解釋評估，我們在本文中解決了這一問題。由於這些方案旨在標記需要審查的主張，而不是輸出欺騙判決，因此我們不對分類準確性進行基準測試；相反，我們通過測量工具在十個當代大型語言模型和重複運行中的前提和結論評估的一致性來評估方法論的\emph{可靠性}。我們發現，對於明確的欺騙，方案檢測的穩定性非常高，而在更模糊的情報風格敘事中，則以可解釋的方式優雅地降級。
